Mr. Ravindra Singh Rawat, learned
Legal Aid Counsel for respondent no. 2.
2. The present Criminal Revision is
accompanied by a Delay Condonation
Application seeking condonation of a
delay of 130 days in filing the revision.
3. Learned Legal Aid Counsel
appearing for respondent no. 2 orally
opposed the Delay Condonation
Application, contending that no
satisfactory explanation has been
furnished for the delay.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist
submitted that talks for an amicable
settlement between the parties were
underway and, therefore, the revision
could not be filed earlier. It is submitted
that the present revision was preferred
only after the settlement talks ultimately
failed.
5. Having considered the reasons
stated in the application and the
submissions advanced on behalf of the
revisionist, this Court finds the
explanation for the delay to be
satisfactory. Accordingly, the delay of
130 days in filing the revision is
condoned and the Delay Condonation
Application is allowed.

6. The present Criminal Revision has
been filed against the order dated
03.10.2025 passed by the learned
Principal Judge, Family Court,
Haldwani, District Nainital in Misc.
Criminal Case No. 31 of 2025 under
Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, whereby the
learned Family Court allowed the
application for interim maintenance filed
by respondent no. 2 and awarded
interim maintenance of Rs. 8,000/- per
month from the date of filing of the
application, i.e., 20.01.2025.
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist
submitted that the revisionist is earning
only about Rs. 12,000/- per month and
is not in a financial position to pay the
amount of maintenance awarded by the
Family Court. It is further submitted
that respondent no. 2 is residing in the
same house as the revisionist and,
therefore, the amount of interim
maintenance awarded is on the higher
side.
8. Per contra, learned Legal Aid
Counsel appearing for respondent no. 2-
wife submitted that respondent no. 2 is
residing in the house of her parents-in-law. He further submitted that the father
of the revisionist has instituted a suit
seeking to evict the revisionist from his
property; however, despite the pendency
of the said suit, the revisionist continues
to reside in the same house. It is
contended that the said suit has been
instituted only with a view to create a
defence and avoid the liability of paying
maintenance to respondent no. 2-wife.
Learned counsel further submitted that
the revisionist is running a mobile shop
at Haldwani and is the proprietor thereof
and, therefore, possesses sufficient
means to maintain his wife.
9. Having heard learned counsel for

the parties and upon perusal of the
record, this Court finds that the
impugned order has been passed after
considering the material available on
record and the prima facie financial
needs of respondent no. 2. The grant of
interim maintenance is intended to
provide immediate financial support to
the claimant spouse during the
pendency of the proceedings.
10. At this stage, this Court does not
find any illegality, perversity,
jurisdictional error, or material
irregularity in the impugned order
warranting interference in exercise of
revisional jurisdiction.
11. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision
is dismissed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall
stand disposed of accordingly.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
